name: Infollion Research Services Limited
sector: Expert networks and specialist research services
summary: Infollion is a real, capital-efficient expert-network service business, not a proven winner-take-most software platform. Six-year revenue and gross-profit growth are strong, but discounts, staff investment and slower collections now separate sales growth from owner earnings. BQS 6.20, Growth Quality Score 6.75 and IAS 4.85 indicate adequate business quality with an insufficient assessed return at the ₹150.80 official 19 October 2026 close. The funded base case returns 12.45% versus a 15% hurdle; its assumption-dependent hurdle entry is ₹134.78. The bear survives financially but implies roughly 47% equity downside. priority: Research watchlist / wait for better evidenced setup

quote.status: Official final close, not live executable quote

material_facts: Unmodified audit, explicit RPT disclosure and exact explanations for consolidated subtotal/ESOP presentation differences.
Founder control near 51.6%; ₹1.27 crore MD remuneration and related software supplier require continuing scrutiny.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Repeated recognition corrections and software capitalization judgment prevent a strong stewardship designation.
factor_audit.rationale: Adequate but not exemplary evidence; no substantiated diversion or minority abuse. Auditor change is an appointment, not automatically a suspect resignation.

material_facts: Large curated panel and repeat use of already-paneled experts can lower search time and fulfillment cost.
FY26 gross spread fell to 41.2%; discounts and multi-vendor competition are acknowledged.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Longstanding institutional relationships and access to niche practitioners have real utility.
factor_audit.rationale: Useful matching/process/reputation advantages, but no proven exclusivity or retention cohort demonstrating self-reinforcing pricing power.

material_facts: Five-year restated-to-current revenue CAGR 44.42%, corroborated by 42.13% gross-profit CAGR.
Current H1 revenue growth slowed to 15.56%, after H2 FY26 moderation.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Absolute revenue additions remain substantial; deceleration is not contraction.
factor_audit.rationale: Schedule starting point 9 for ≥30%; −1 for sustained two-half-year slowdown, within maximum adjustment. Medium comparability confidence independently caps at 8, not a second deduction.

material_facts: Core consulting/investment/corporate research needs persist; new Huksa customers and funded international presence offer access beyond a headline TAM.
Three newer verticals exceeded ₹1 crore in FY26 and Huksa reports 55 clients by H1 FY27.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Non-India remains single-digit revenue and AI may displace generic research or compress budgets.
factor_audit.rationale: Multiple evidenced avenues with credible funding, but demand and monetization are neither contracted nor SaaS-like.

material_facts: Three- and five-year aggregate incremental operating returns near 40%/46% exceed an assumed 13–16% INR cost-of-capital range.
FY26 one-year incremental proxy falls to about 0.4% while software and new-team spending continue.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Full-expense software alternative still supports strong historical capital efficiency; small physical asset base is genuine, not automatically poor evidence.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed old-business returns versus unseasoned latest investment. Historical IC/NOPAT bridge is scoreable without inventing cohorts; current uncertainty prevents 7–8 durability credit.

material_facts: FY24–26 reported ratio-of-sums CFO/PAT is 0.750×, and treasury/ESOP/prior-capitalization-adjusted sensitivity is 0.580×.
H1 FY27 CFO/PAT is 0.192×; unbilled was 53.4% of March receivables.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Small annual overdue balances and positive multi-year FCF counter an unsupported bad-debt or fraud conclusion.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed realization, rapid expert payouts and unbilled balances; seasonality explanation preserved, not treated as resolved cash. No persistent-value-destruction override.

material_facts: ₹43.12 crore reviewed September liquid assets and zero debt support a large conservative reserve.
Bear/base/bull remain above cash floor after haircut, no-collection bridge, old employee reserve and Thermium payment.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Linked severe collection/cost shock can still breach required cash; acquisition appetite can consume surplus.
factor_audit.rationale: Strong demonstrable resilience from recent public accounts, without demanding private daily statements or inventing facilities.

material_facts: Revenue passed ₹100 crore and three new verticals achieved real but small sales.
Headcount rose 200 to 271 while operating EBITDA barely grew; FY27 profit still below comparable period.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Management disclosed cost/margin and collection explanations rather than making a precise margin-recovery promise.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed scaling delivery: strong commercial growth but latest reinvestment productivity is not established.

material_facts: FY26 PAT only rose 2.23% despite 29.78% revenue growth; treasury/prior income and software capitalization matter.
H1 FY27 PAT fell 7.67%, or about 2.2% after management prior-item adjustment.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Underlying business remains profitable, dilution from existing options is small and no large acquisition boost is inserted.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed recurring per-share earnings progression. Normalization expensing current software keeps economics separate from reported profit.

material_facts: Supported base return 12.45% is 2.55 percentage points below the 15% hurdle.
Base hurdle entry is about ₹134.78 versus ₹150.80 observed close.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Bull outcome is materially higher, but needs 20% growth and 12× exit EBIT.
factor_audit.rationale: v3.0 return spread −4 to <−2 percentage points maps exactly to R4. No return penalty for a funding gap that is not present.

material_facts: Bear cash remains funded but terminal value about ₹80.42 is 46.67% below entry.
Balance-sheet liquidity and modest fixed capital provide survival support.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: No audited current client concentration or guarantee of orderly exit; combined severe shocks can exhaust cash floor.
factor_audit.rationale: Survival is better than share-price protection. Material equity impairment despite available cash warrants a middle score, not a distressed classification.

material_facts: 15% hurdle requires about 13.54% annual revenue growth under fixed base margins and 9× EBIT exit.
Observed near-term growth 15.56% is compatible, but base normalized cost/cash case returns less than hurdle.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Multiple/growth and software-cost sensitivities leave limited margin for forecasting error.
factor_audit.rationale: Price is not an extreme-growth valuation, but a good execution case rather than independent conservative cases is needed.

material_facts: All 60 official sessions show trades; conservative 5% theoretical exit is 6.45 sessions.
ST settlement, ₹60,320 lot and three successive near-limit down closes impair implementation.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Twenty-day and sixty-day whole-lot capacity exist in aggregate; stock is not evidenced suspended or permanently untradeable.
factor_audit.rationale: Starting band score 5 for >5–10 days; explicit −1 for ST/lot granularity and −1 for consecutive near-limit closes. No assumed executable spread.

gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.reason: No substantiated severe minority harm. Founder concentration, compensation, related software purchases and repeated accounting corrections need continued review; RPT subtotal gap is fully explained by disclosed intercompany eliminations.

gates.name: Financial reliability
gates.reason: Core financial statements reconcile. Pre-IPO restatements, tax netting, employee-cost regrouping and ESOP reclassification have explicit bridges. Prior-expert-charge placement remains a bounded .8655 crore normalization ambiguity; forecasts use conservative current operating economics and cash, without adding back the disputed charge. No material unexplained balance-sheet gap remains in reviewed records.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.reason: Recent public liquidity and conservative reserve bridge fund all principal scenarios without rescue or assumed tax recovery. Severe combined stress can breach, but no actual default or current shortfall established.

gates.name: Tradability
gates.reason: Active ST series and verified trades; position-sized capacity exists, but lot/circuit/queue constraints make immediate exit uncertain. Not a verified effectively-untradeable condition.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Infollion is a real, capital-efficient expert-network service business, not a proven winner-take-most software platform. Six-year revenue and gross-profit growth are strong, but discounts, staff investment and slower collections now separate sales growth from owner earnings. BQS 6.20, Growth Quality Score 6.75 and IAS 4.85 indicate adequate business quality with an insufficient assessed return at the ₹150.80 official 19 October 2026 close. The funded base case returns 12.45% versus a 15% hurdle; its assumption-dependent hurdle entry is ₹134.78. The bear survives financially but implies roughly 47% equity downside. No fraud, default or automatic asset-light penalty is inferred. Core repeat-client spend, current concentration, technology commissioning and cash collection would matter more than panel growth alone. The thesis is an asset-light growth/value watchlist, not an evidence-backed compounder. A network can make sourcing more useful without making client contracts exclusive. Financial resources are genuine support: the latest reviewed balance sheet is recent enough to underpin conservative stress analysis. The decisive risk is monetization rather than physical capacity. More calls, experts and employees must produce recurring net value added and cash after development spending. A lower market price alone cannot cure weaker customer economics, but an entry materially below the modeled hurdle threshold could improve the setup if collections and compliance remain sound. This is research, not a trade instruction.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Exact issuer: Infollion Research Services Limited; NSE SME INFOLLION; ISIN INE0NNZ01013; current CIN L73100HR2009PLC126450. Its former private-company/legal registration references in the prospectus are not a second issuer. The US subsidiary, Infollion Research Services Corp., is wholly owned and consolidated; the 19% Thermium investment is a financial investment, not consolidated sales. Accounting uses Indian GAAP Accounting Standards in the Companies (Accounting Standards) framework, commonly called AS/non-Ind AS, with AS 21 consolidation, AS 9 revenue and AS 26 software recognition. Do not relabel it Ind AS.

Information cutoff is 20 October 2026, Asia/Kolkata. Source retrieval on 21 October does not authorize hindsight; the October 21 quote and any later events are excluded. Price is the official 19 October ST close ₹150.80, not live or guaranteed executable. Basic issued shares are 9,706,759, giving ₹146.38 crore market capitalization; 19,574 outstanding options are modeled separately. Horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, five calendar years. The nominal pretax equity hurdle is 15%, with 12/18% sensitivity. ₹5 lakh is only an illustrative liquidity reference.

G1 Conditional: no proven abuse, but founder control/RPTs/accounting corrections merit scrutiny. G2 Conditional: explicitly reconciled presentation and scope changes permit analysis, while normalization ambiguity is conservatively bounded. G3 Clear: recent cash covers modeled stress without rescue. G4 Conditional: traded ST shares with circuit and lot constraints. These are not guarantees. Confidence is High on exact security and official liquidity observations; Medium on accounting comparability, governance, historical capital efficiency and model inputs; Low on core customer cohorts and pricing power. The investment conclusion is only Medium-confidence because its main uncertainty is future operating economics, not source retrieval.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
All 13 canonical factors are assigned once. BQS uses GOV 6, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 7, CAP 6, CASH 5, BAL 8 and EXEC 6. GQS reuses REV/DUR/CAP/CASH and adds EARN 5. IAS reuses final unrounded BQS once with R 4, D 5, P 6 and L 3. Exact Decimal weights, contributions, raw/final totals, coverage and missing-factor bounds are embedded below. BQS is 6.20; GQS is 6.75; IAS is 4.85. All have 100% scored coverage, but this does not mean all possible business information is known. No numeric override is applied: none of GOV/CAP/CASH reaches a severe-failure threshold and G3 does not fail.

REV starts at 9 for >30% comparable five-year growth, then falls one point for the sustained latest two-half-year deceleration; Medium comparability confidence also limits it to 8, not a second deduction. CAP is not inferred from tiny physical assets or a headline ROCE: both aggregate incremental capital and fully expensed technology alternatives are calculated. Its 6 reflects strong past returns but mixed latest reinvestment. R follows the exact −2.55 percentage-point return spread band. L begins at 5 for 6.45 theoretical days, then has two disclosed implementation deductions. Evidence gaps do not become neutral scores; unknown cohort metrics remain explicitly ND, but available multi-year evidence is sufficient for bounded factor judgments.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Clients pay Infollion to identify, vet and arrange relevant practitioners for research, diligence, strategy and related engagements. The customer base includes consulting firms, investment organizations and corporates. Revenue is service income recognized when obligations are satisfied; completed but not yet invoiced services are unbilled receivables. Experts are independent practitioners, not inventory or owned productive assets. The company pays expert fees and retains a spread before research staff, sales, travel, data subscriptions, compliance, software development and taxes.

FY26 reported service revenue was ₹100.32 crore and expert fees ₹58.97 crore, leaving ₹41.35 crore gross profit. Calling the full ₹100 crore a SaaS revenue base would obscure the expert-cost pass-through. Equally, calling gross profit a contractual platform take rate would overstate precision: call duration, practitioner rates, waived calls, training projects and discounted high-volume work all affect the blend. There is no disclosed gross booking value beyond recognized revenue or separate principal-agent reassessment to apply. The analysis preserves statutory sales and uses gross profit as the economic cross-check.

India remains the commercial center. FY26 export service revenue ₹6.55 crore is not the same as calls fulfilled by overseas experts; management says more than one-third of business involved experts abroad. H1 FY27 non-India business remains a single-digit sales share. Huksa offers practitioner-led corporate learning and development; AI evaluation, syndicated sessions, tools and APIs are newer initiatives. Thermium is an initial engineering-consulting investment with ₹0.60 crore paid and ₹0.60 crore still committed. There is no separate speculative value for these initiatives. Collection is slower than fulfillment: management reports expert payment within three days while client receivables were about 79 days on an ending-half-year denominator in September.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is cumulative sourcing knowledge, a curated panel, fast response, relevant matches and trust in compliance. Mechanism: a richer taxonomy and repeat use of specialists should reduce search time and increase fulfillment. Evidence: management reports 136,461 panel experts, 20,736 FY26 calls and >80% revenue from already-paneled experts. Durability depends on keeping profiles useful and matching reliably as demand changes. Failure modes are multi-homing experts, clients spreading projects among vendors, price concessions, talented staff leaving and competitors using better data or AI tools. None of the reported panel statistics establishes active utilization, exclusivity, client net retention or a scalable software contribution margin.

GLG, AlphaSights and Guidepoint are economically relevant operating comparators, not public-market P/E comparables. Their own materials describe matching technology, human service teams and compliance controls. AlphaSights emphasizes expert/background screening and client protection; Guidepoint offers client-specific preapproval, supervised calls and usage oversight; GLG pairs its network with technology and compliance. These are large established alternatives against which Infollion must win specific relationships. No private peer revenue, margin or valuation is invented, and generic staffing-company multiples are not substituted.

The FY23 prospectus reported top-five customers at 80.38% of revenue and top-ten at 87.76%. Current shares are ND, so those dated figures are not mislabeled FY26 concentration. Diversification into new geographies and Huksa is progress, but each new vertical only recently passed ₹1 crore. The company says most revenue is repeat business, yet repeat spend can be cyclical, discount-dependent or concentrated. Huksa's approximate 60% repeat rate is not a core-network retention cohort. MOAT 5 recognizes useful processes and institutional relationships while withholding a structural network-effect premium. Compliance creates trust and operational friction, but it is also a costly entry requirement that rivals possess.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The consistently labeled history uses IPO-restated FY21–23 revenue ₹15.9701/21.9846/35.0309 crore, then audited FY24–26 revenue ₹51.7483/77.3032/100.3197 crore. Five-year CAGR is 44.42% and three-year CAGR 42.01%; annual additions are ₹6.0145, ₹13.0463, ₹16.7174, ₹25.5549 and ₹23.0165 crore. Ten-year CAGR is ND because eleven observations were not established. The company's 43.5% three-year headline uses original FY23 ₹33.9427 crore; the difference to the restated comparator is explained by ₹1.0882 crore unbilled revenue, not silently ignored.

Gross profit grows from ₹7.13 crore in FY21 to ₹41.35 crore in FY26, a 42.13% five-year CAGR, so gross sales growth is not merely inflated expert pass-through. However, FY26 sales rose 29.78% while gross profit rose 17.21%; expert-cost share increased. H2 FY26 sales ₹49.23 crore were below H1 ₹51.09 crore. H1 FY27 sales ₹59.04 crore rose 15.56% year over year and 19.94% sequentially, whereas PAT fell 7.67% year over year. TTM revenue is ₹108.27 crore and PAT ₹12.16 crore, calculated latest FY plus current H1 minus prior H1. No invented TTM CFO or quarterly annualization is used.

The core business appears organic in the reviewed perimeter: US service sales are eliminated within consolidation, and Thermium's 19% financial stake is not added to operating revenue. A fully quantified volume/price/mix, paid-call and client-count bridge is not disclosed. Panel expansion and overseas-expert sourcing are not substitutes for sales volume or foreign-customer revenue. REV 8 retains genuine commercial progress, applying only the permitted single trajectory deduction. It does not award points for a global gig-economy TAM.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Growth quality is 6.75, below the threshold for a high-quality compounder designation even before the moat requirement. Infollion has real accessible customers and has scaled without financial debt or heavy equipment. The relevant reinvestment is people, expert sourcing, client acquisition, software, compliance and working capital, not factory utilization. The core matching service can grow by more client teams, a wider expert pool, more sessions per project and new formats. Each must retain gross value after expert fees and acquire collections at acceptable cost.

The three-year incremental NOPAT/committed-capital proxy is 39.92% and five-year proxy 45.98%; the corresponding fully expensed software alternative remains strong after removing software from both earnings and capital. These are meaningful positive denominators with a line-by-line IC bridge, not ratios inflated by negative incremental capital. They include retained software under development, current operating assets and employee provisions, and exclude treasury and tax assets. The FY26 financing-side check is equity ₹67.3348 crore + deferred tax ₹0.0652 crore + current tax provision ₹0.0546 crore − cash ₹43.4850 crore − tax assets ₹2.4144 crore − accrued interest ₹0.0017 crore = ₹21.5535 crore, matching operating IC ₹21.5534 crore within ₹1,000 source rounding. Expensed research/sales labor is already charged in earnings. The analyst cost-of-capital comparison is 13–16% nominal INR, separate from the 15% equity hurdle. Neither the accounting return nor this assumed range proves a project IRR.

The latest-year increment is the counterevidence: NOPAT barely rises while committed capital increases ₹3.86 crore, giving about 0.4%. Much spending supports newer teams and a platform that has not begun amortizing. Those investments may eventually earn good returns, but published core cohorts and separately attributable new-vertical profitability are ND. CAP 6 therefore reflects mixed current reinvestment, not a penalty for asset-light economics. The base cash model assumes 10% annual revenue growth, continued technology spending at 2% of revenue, 85 receivable days and no new financing. A weak-market case cuts revenue and gross margin together with delayed collections. These models demonstrate funding capacity, not proof that growth will occur.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The founder-controlled business has a long operating history, but governance must be assessed through decisions rather than ownership percentage. FY26 MD remuneration was ₹1.27 crore, about 10% of consolidated PAT. The AGM notice proposed a ₹1.80 crore annual limit; notice alone is not proof of approval and no approved new expense is assumed. Related-party software services from Simplifii Labs were ₹1.106 crore in FY25 and ₹0.04 crore in FY26; named director links are disclosed. The board describes RPTs as arm's-length and ordinary-course, which is management's statement rather than independent price verification.

The consolidated RPT table prints a ₹10.1902 crore total although visible non-intercompany rows sum to ₹1.7706 crore. The ₹8.4196 crore difference exactly equals disclosed US subsidiary expert reimbursements ₹7.9675 crore, support fee ₹0.3984 crore and interest ₹0.0537 crore eliminated in consolidation. This resolves the economically important difference as a carried-over subtotal, not unidentified leakage; an issuer-corrected total was not located. Statutory auditor PRANV & Associates was appointed for five years in September 2025. The FY26 opinion is unmodified and software capitalization is a key audit matter. Neither an auditor change nor a clean opinion proves a governance conclusion by itself.

Observable promises-versus-delivery: the ₹100 crore sales milestone was achieved in FY26, and US/MENA/Huksa each exceeded ₹1 crore; expected margin recovery was not dated, so no invented missed numerical guidance is created. The platform is being used/tested with additional features under development, while the ₹6.35 crore September carrying amount remains unamortized. Hiring expanded but profit productivity has yet to follow. Management explicitly acknowledges aggressive pricing and Q4 volume weakness and offers a Q2 timing explanation for receivables. These explanations are preserved alongside the negative data. Current primary pledge and complete latest shareholder-file detail were not retrieved, so no verified-zero-pledge claim is made.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The complete six-year historical table and current interim are embedded in the canonical, with scope, audit basis, gross profit, operating EBITDA/EBIT, PAT, normalization, EPS, CFO, reported capex, FCF, cash, debt, equity, receivables/unbilled balances, capital and share counts. FY24–26 cumulative CFO ₹25.30 crore divided by PAT ₹33.73 crore is 0.750×, not an average of annual ratios. Removing all disclosed liquid-fund gains, adding noncash ESOP reserve transfers and removing prior-period noncash software capitalization gives a conservative 0.580× sensitivity, not a restated audited cash-flow statement. The earlier treasury/ESOP-only sensitivity is 0.622× and is retained as an intermediate step. FY26 prior-period salary capitalization requires the paired analytical reclassification CFO −₹1.4137 crore / CFI +₹1.4137 crore; ESOP requires CFO +₹0.3292 crore / CFF −₹0.3292 crore. Both leave total cash unchanged, and reported CFO/PAT remains 0.750×. No separate expert-charge removal is made in this cash sensitivity. Cash capex belongs in investing flow, not an explanation for low CFO. H1 CFO ₹1.30 crore is constrained by ₹7.08 crore receivable growth and ₹1.77 crore extra tax advances, partly funded by payables/current liabilities.

Several reconciliation traps are explicit. FY24's ₹3.3092 crore opening-unbilled correction enters both the old-opening receivable change and cash-flow addback; deleting only the addback understates cash. FY25's later balance sheet nets taxes/GST, reducing assets and liabilities by about ₹4.12 crore without changing equity or cash. October FY26 comparatives move ₹0.0979 crore between payroll and other expense with no PBT effect. FY26 CFF ₹0.3390 crore includes ₹0.3292 crore noncash ESOP reserve transfer, whereas actual exercise cash is ₹0.009787 crore; the corresponding CFO addback uses net reserve change, so a reclassification preserves total cash. Forecasts include only genuine option exercise cash.

FY26 software additions ₹2.8905 crore include ₹1.4137 crore prior-period salaries; current-period development is ₹1.4768 crore. Note 13 nets the prior salary credit against ₹0.8655 crore prior expert expense to give ₹0.5482 crore prior income, while management also describes the expert charge within cost of sales. The analysis does not remove it twice or assert an undisclosed loss: normalization removes all other income and fully expenses current development, leaving the gross-margin addback as a bounded management alternative. March unbilled revenue is ₹9.81 crore, 53.4% of receivables; only ₹0.10 crore is reported over six months. September current ageing is ND. Bank charges, not borrowing interest, comprise finance costs. Operating rentals remain operating costs; no fabricated lease debt or separate IP/property value is added.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹150.80 and 9,706,759 shares, market value is ₹146.38 crore. Reported FY26 P/E is about 11.5× and TTM P/E about 12.0×, but these capitalize treasury income and favorably timed software accounting unless normalized. The model therefore uses operating EBIT after bank charges and full ongoing technology cash expense, taxes at 25%, linked ONWC and hardware capex. No separate software value or hypothetical Thermium exit is added. Cash begins from September's reviewed liquid resources with a 5% liquidity haircut, twenty days of operating cash expense with zero receipts, and full reservation of old employee liabilities. Tax refunds are not assumed collected. The remaining ₹0.60 crore Thermium commitment is paid once. Cash required for operations, max(₹12 crore,12% of annualized sales), is retained at terminal rather than given to shareholders.

Bear/base/bull annual rows run from 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031. Fiscal stubs use actual days, including 366-day financial years; no post-terminal cash gap controls the return. The October 2031 exit explicitly applies a multiple to the full FY32 annualized forward fiscal operating rate, not to FY32 profit already earned or trailing October earnings. Required cash uses the same full annualized FY32 sales rate. Only the actual fiscal stub contributes cash before exit; no post-exit cash is included. Existing options exercise with real cash and modest ownership dilution; dividends and new debt/rescue are zero. Bear has weaker sales, 38% gross spread, sticky payroll, 120-day collections and 7× EBIT exit. Base uses 10% growth, 41% gross spread, gradual payroll efficiency, 85 days and 9× EBIT. Bull needs 20% growth, a 43% gross spread, more operating leverage, 70 days and 12× exit. All three are financeable under the disclosed reserves, not simply assumed funded.

Their terminal prices are approximately ₹80.42/271.09/685.85 and pretax annualized returns −11.82%/12.45%/35.38%. The base falls short of 15%; its conditional entry thresholds are ₹153.82/134.78/118.50 at 12/15/18% hurdles. These are assumption-dependent, not observable fair values. Reverse expectations require about 13.54% growth with the other base assumptions fixed. The full growth×multiple grid, linked margin/collection/cost shocks and 1/2/5% execution-cost tests are embedded. A perpetual DCF is not forced given cash classification and software timing; terminal-value share is NA because no DCF is used. Any stress breaching cash-floor requirements has null return and entry fields, not an investable negative-cash target.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is that Infollion is an efficient but contestable intermediation service whose apparent network moat is mostly accumulated labor and relationships. Major customers can use several networks and demand concessions. Experts can work elsewhere. Management's own discounted engagements and client-development calls show that retention can be purchased at a lower spread. AI can increase expert validation demand, but it can also eliminate basic discovery calls and move value to richer data platforms. A compliance breach or confidentiality failure could lose institutional clients precisely when fixed staff costs are difficult to reduce.

The bear links reduced revenue and gross margin with sticky payroll and 120-day receivables. It preserves survival but produces ₹80.42 per share, about 46.67% below the reference price. That is permanent earnings/multiple impairment, not merely temporary quotation volatility. Liquid assets are valuable but do not fully protect equity purchased above cash value; new acquisitions and prolonged product development can consume them. A separate combined customer-loss/150-day collection/₹10 crore cost scenario and severe ₹30 crore cash-use scenario test funding further. Any breach invalidates ordinary modeled returns until financing is separately evidenced; no rescue proceeds or legal ability to raise them are invented.

The thesis-break variable is sustained retained gross profit and cash per client project after expert sourcing, staff and software. If gross margin falls below about 38%, receivables stay above 100–120 days without explanation, development remains uncommissioned, or client loss leaves staff underutilized, strong past revenue CAGR would not protect intrinsic value. Impairment risk is Moderate-to-High because liquidity supports solvency but client concentration, cash realization and execution constraints can still create large equity loss. Neither the ST designation nor historical accounting corrections alone is an allegation of fraud.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold equity outcome requires 37.97% annual compounding over five years, and tenfold requires 58.49%; over ten years those rates fall to 17.46% and 25.89%. Infollion's reported historical sales CAGR exceeds some of those rates, but margins have compressed, treasury affects PAT and current growth is slower. Extrapolating the old sales CAGR into an equal stock return would ignore starting price, reinvestment, diluted claims and exit multiple.

The explicitly optimistic five-year bull produces about 4.55× terminal wealth, not an underwritten 5× result. It already combines 20% annual sales expansion, a recovery in retained spread, material personnel leverage, faster collections and a 12× EBIT exit. A larger outcome would require stronger persistent unit economics, monetization of new offerings or more multiple support. None is established by the 136,461-expert panel count, a global TAM or the Thermium stake. No probability or expected multibagger rank is assigned.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Core-client concentration and spend: request latest top-five/top-ten shares, paying clients and same-client revenue. FY23 top-ten 87.76% is the only dated baseline, not current diversification proof.
2. Gross profit and pricing: FY26 margin 41.2%, H1 FY27 40.9%. Investigate sustained <38% or continued >5-point gap versus historic economics; distinguish free/discount calls from a contractual take rate.
3. Collections: September receivables ₹25.45 crore and roughly 79 ending-balance days; seek subsequent cash and billed/unbilled ageing. Persistent >100–120 days or new aged balances require model revision, not just a timing explanation.
4. Cash conversion: H1 CFO/PAT 0.192× versus FY24–26 0.750× reported. Monitor full-year recovery with treasury gains and ESOP movements bridged separately.
5. Technology: September development asset ₹6.35 crore; obtain commissioning, remaining cost, amortization life and expense/capitalization split. Monitor full cash development cost, not only reported D&A.
6. Staff productivity: September 280 employees versus 271 in March; compare revenue and gross profit per employee and new-vertical contribution, not headcount alone.
7. Cash allocation: monitor liquid resources versus operating floor, the ₹0.60 crore residual Thermium commitment, any acquisition and actual recipient/perimeter. No assumed tax release or unannounced deal funding.
8. Governance and diluted claims: obtain latest pledge/shareholding filing, auditor/recognition follow-up, RPT subtotal correction and annual remuneration decision; monitor only actual granted options and exercise cash.
9. Compliance and AI: track material client complaints, control failures, platform usage and paid AI-validation/syndicated revenue. New features are not revenue until disclosed.
10. Execution: refresh official 20/60-session volumes, active series, lot, price band and live quotes before any implementation decision. A series upgrade or short volume burst is not guaranteed exit liquidity.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification under v3.0: Insufficient return for identified risks. BQS 6.20 lies in the ≥6 to <8 quality band and IAS 4.85 is below 5.5. GQS 6.75 means growth has been substantial but latest cash/profit reinvestment evidence is mixed. The action category is Research watchlist / wait for a better evidenced setup, not eligible-for-investment endorsement and not a sell instruction for an undisclosed holding.

An evidence-backed compounder designation is not earned: BQS is below 8, GQS below 7, MOAT below 7 and CASH below 6. The company is not classified distressed because the public cash bridge funds the principal linked cases; it is not classified Avoid-governance without substantiated severe adverse evidence. Conditional gates highlight what remains to verify rather than conflating all warnings with misconduct.

On the modeled base, around ₹135 meets the 15% hurdle before material execution friction, but that is conditional on costs, working capital, dilution and exit valuation, not a recommended order price. Better collections, independently supported current client diversification and technology commissioning could justify more confidence or different assumptions. Conversely, a margin/collection deterioration or costly acquisition would lower value even if the quote falls. Refresh both financials and lot/series conditions for a different position size. This dossier contains no personalized allocation or transaction instruction.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source register and claim-level evidence ledger below identify primary disclosures, dates, precise financial-statement locators, original URLs and original-byte hashes. Historical figures are taken from the final prospectus, annual reports and latest exchange-filed results, not aggregator snapshots. Company forecasts, operational claims and explanations are labeled management statements; arithmetic and forecast assumptions are separate. Qualitative undated company/competitor web policies are corroboration only and do not establish post-cutoff quantitative facts.

Material open questions: current core client concentration, paid/free-call cohorts and repeat spend; September billed/unbilled ageing and subsequent collections; full expert-payment prior-period placement; software commissioning and future maintenance/amortization; current primary pledge/ownership details; updated remuneration approval; complete historical use-of-proceeds schedule and contingent lease maturities. The analysis bounds known recognition/presentation issues, keeps amounts visible and avoids counting the same correction twice. No management contact or unrequested communication was undertaken.

Model assumptions are nominal INR, 25% normalized tax, no automatic interest income on retained cash, zero dividends and no future rescue/debt. Ongoing software is fully expensed economically, already captured in cash, not deducted again as capex. Hardware capex, working-capital absorption, Thermium payment, option proceeds and operating cash reserves reconcile separately. Per-share dilution is holder dilution rather than share-count growth. Historical CAP is an aggregate accounting proxy with a full capital bridge, not cohort evidence.

The analytical backups intentionally contain no original PDFs, raw web pages, OCR, screenshots, shareholder lists or personal identifiers. Safe financial extracts, source URLs/hashes and reproducible models remain. Offline reproduction verifies calculation consistency and byte-identical artifacts, not fresh authenticity of original filings. Fresh source authentication requires retrieving originals independently and comparing hashes. Facts and assumptions may change after the cutoff; historical volume and modeled returns do not assure execution or future results.
